title: One Split or Several Folds?
description: Course activity for Exercise 4: compare a single train/test split with cross-validation across a fixed set of sample sizes, seeds, and fold counts, holding the KNN model (k=20) fixed.
instructions: Choose a sample size, a random seed, and a number of folds. The random seed changes only how the same participants are partitioned, not which participants are included. Compare the single-split test score with the cross-validation fold scores below.
reflectionPrompts: How much does the result change when only the split changes?
Is the variability larger with 50 participants or with the full sample?
Could two researchers using different splits reach different conclusions?
Does increasing the number of folds always improve the model?
What changes when the number of folds increases?
